title: fix(searchBox): handling pasting event with contextual menu.

comments.body: @maxiloc I think we figured a more advanced way to handle that in https://github.com/algolia/instant-search-demo/pull/20 mentioned by @vvo in the issue.
Ok cool, I am modifying that

> Ok cool, I am modifying that

:+1: awesome
I am not sure there's an "input" magical event in pure DOM

Should be pretty-well supported:
http://caniuse.com/#feat=input-event

But be careful, the order in which `input`, `change`, `keypress`, `keyup` and `keydown` are fired is tricky.

@maxiloc If you want to see how we did it in the demo: https://github.com/algolia/instant-search-demo/pull/20/files

@vvo's suggestion works pretty well because it also supports cutting and deleting with the mouse, plus the case where someone might paste text on to the end of an existing query.

> But be careful, the order in which input, change, keypress, keyup and keydown are fired is tricky.

So I wonder, @pixelastic can't we just use 'input' event for everything (it would handle keyup, change, paste..).

Then the only missing part would be that on IE9, deleting would not produce a new search, we can fix that separately.
I rebased, the handling of event is a bit different than jquery but it works
